walkthroughs.body_html:
If God is omnipotent and omnibenevolent, why is there evil?

Christians distinguish moral evil (caused by humans) and natural evil (earthquakes, disease).

One response: humans have free will. Real love and goodness require choice, and choice means evil is possible. Adam and Eve's misuse of free will is called the Fall.

Christians believe Jesus will return and judge the living and the dead (Matthew 25 — sheep and goats).

Those who showed love — feeding the hungry, visiting prisoners — are welcomed; those who didn't are turned away.

The criteria are both faith in Jesus and a life that reflects God's love.

Heaven is eternal life with God. Many Christians see it as spiritual rather than literally streets of gold.

Hell is eternal separation from God. Some see it as literal fire, others as the absence of God's love.

Roman Catholics also believe in purgatory — a state of cleansing before entering heaven. Protestants generally reject this teaching.
